To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the promoters of the fimbrial subunits of Bordetella are unusual, and that BvgA activates these promoters through an atypical interaction with the RNA polymerase holoenzyme.

Bordetella pertusis fimbrial promoters contain an unusual C‐stretch that is essential to promoter function; the length of this stretch is optimized to give maximal transcriptional activity; the optimal C‐stretch is conserved among three different fimbrial promoters, and is occupied by BvgA; the BvgA‐DNA interaction is unusual, in that BvgA occupies the centre of a −35‐like sequence, and the C‐stretch may be involved in this unusual interaction.
BvgA binding at a site that is not a canonical −35 sequence is required for maximal activation of fimbrial promoters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the unusual architecture of the promoters of B. pertussis fims genes, and the mechanism by which the BvgA transcriptional activator binds to these promoters.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BvgA‐activated promoters of B. pertussis fim genes are unique, with a promoter architecture that is distinct from that of other known BvgA‐regulated promoters.
BvgA is a global virulence regulator that controls the expression of a large number of genes in B. pertussis by binding to their promoter regions.
the fim promoters are novel and unique, and are not related to the promoters of other B. pertussis virulence genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the fim promoters have been shaped by the need to optimize the balance between the requirements for phase variation and for high transcriptional activity, with the result that their structure is highly unusual.
BvgA binding to a promoter can be a substitute for a −35 element, but that it must be accompanied by the presence of an upstream BvgA‐responsive element.

, in addition to phase variation, the C‐stretch also serves as a novel regulatory element, by providing a BvgA‐specific high affinity binding site, and that this binding site is located at a non‐canonical position in the promoter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the promoters of fimbrial subunits are highly conserved in terms of both their structure and their BvgA binding properties.
, while the fim promoters are activated by BvgA, their architecture is distinct from that of other BvgA‐activated genes.
the promoters of the three fimbrial subunits have been optimized to function together, and that the C‐stretch has been selected for its capacity to bind BvgA, which in turn activates the promoters.
